context: A systematic trading firm. ~200 quantitative researchers, full tick-level market data, in-house execution, production ML infrastructure and a research platform that replicates any result before it trades. Horizon is days to weeks. Work is judged on whether a signal survives transaction costs, has capacity, and is not already crowded. Findings go to a research committee that will re-run them independently. Building a ten-year intraday dataset is a normal quarter's work here.
seed: Do round-lot orders identify retail flow that is profitable to trade against?
plan_A:
Hypothesis: round-lot (100-share multiple) imbalance is tested as a retail proxy, not assumed, since algo slicing and odd-lot rules confound it. Primary: daily signed round-lot order-flow imbalance (RLOIB) predicts negative one-day-ahead returns, attenuating or flipping by day 20. Tradeable version: a long-short book fading RLOIB earns alpha against factors including short-term reversal (STR), surviving a spread-plus-impact cost model. Falsification: if RLOIB's incremental Fama-MacBeth coefficient (controlling for all-lot imbalance ALLOIB and subpenny retail imbalance RETOIB) has |t|<2.0 at every horizon, the lot filter adds nothing; if it survives but net-of-cost long-short alpha has t<2.0 under base costs, the effect is real but unharvestable.

Data: NYSE Daily TAQ (Trades, NBBO, Master) via WRDS, 2 Jan 2015–present (odd lots reportable from Dec 2013); 2010–2013 extension is a caveated stability check. CRSP daily returns/prices/shares/exchange/delisting; Compustat book equity lagged 6 months; Ken French daily 5-factor + momentum + STR; IHS Markit (or Ortex) lending fees; Thomson/Refinitiv 13F ownership, lagged 1 quarter; Compustat/IBES earnings dates. Universe: CRSP codes 10/11, NYSE/NYSE American/Nasdaq, price $5–$1000, mkt cap above NYSE 20th percentile, 20-day median dollar volume >$1M; drop 5 days post-IPO, 2 days around splits/distributions, earnings day/day-after in main spec (kept as robustness).

Methodology: clean trades per Holden–Jacobsen (09:30–16:00, correction 00, conditions blank/@/F/I, drop non-positive price/size and >10% deviations from surrounding 20-print median); NBBO filtered for crossed/locked quotes and wide spreads. Sign via Lee–Ready vs. contemporaneous NBBO (no lag), tick test for midpoints; EMO/CLNV as robustness. Lots: odd <100, round = multiples of 100, mixed >100 non-multiple; primary signal uses round lots plus a "retail-plausible" 100–500-share variant; 100-share threshold held fixed despite SEC's later tiered redefinition. RLOIB = (buy−sell round-lot dollars)/(buy+sell), min 20 prints/$50k volume per stock-day, winsorized 1/99% and z-scored cross-sectionally. Companion signals ALLOIB, ODDOIB, RETOIB (subpenny off-exchange classification, validated against venue retail data) built identically. Identification: residualize RLOIB on ALLOIB, ODDOIB, log price/size, rerun regressions on raw and residual; also regress RLOIB on RETOIB in rolling 250-day windows. Predictive regressions: signal at t, entry t+1, returns to t+1+h (h=1,5,20); controls: day-t return, momentum, size, book-to-market, turnover, Amihud illiquidity, volatility, price, round-lot share, institutional ownership. OLS daily cross-section; Newey-West(h+5) SEs cross-checked against Hansen-Hodrick and block bootstrap. Portfolios: daily decile sort fading imbalance, value-weighted, 5-day overlapping holding, dollar- and beta-neutral; costs via TAQ effective half-spread (Corwin-Schultz fallback) plus square-root impact (k=0.5 base, 0.25/1.0 stress, 5% participation cap), Markit short fees (excluding DCBS≥5 or fee>100bps names), 1bp commission; buy/hold-band turnover control (enter decile 1/10, exit 3/8); breakeven cost vs realized cost. Evaluation regresses net returns on 6 standard factors plus in-house ALLOIB/RETOIB factors; bar for real effect: net alpha t>3.0.

Validation: split at end-2019 (zero-commission transition, 2020-21 retail surge); Jan–Mar 2021 reported separately as stress test. Placebos: 250-750 mixed lots, exact-100-only bucket, 5-day-forward signal shift, within-stock-day sign randomization. Sensitivity grid: signing algorithm, NBBO lag, scaling, smoothing, earnings inclusion, deciles vs quintiles, weighting, impact calibration; midquote and t+2–t+6 returns strip bid-ask bounce. Capacity: net alpha across $50M–$5B AUM.

Pitfalls: round lots aren't a clean retail marker (institutional slicing at 100, odd-lot frequency rises with price) — addressed via residualization, price control, RETOIB correlation. Result may be STR relabeled — day-t return control and the STR factor are non-negotiable. Sign may differ by horizon (1-day = liquidity provision; a positive 20-day coefficient is reinterpreted, not failure). Costs likely dominate given concentration in small/cheap/high-retail names — breakeven cost is a headline output. Short leg faces squeeze/borrow-scarcity risk — report long-only-relative-to-universe and short-leg alpha share. Data traps: TAQ symbol/CUSIP-PERMNO changes across corporate actions, the Dec 2013 odd-lot break, later round-lot tiering, sale conditions reintroducing auction volume, delisting fills (-30%/-55%), quote-alignment lookahead.
plan_B:
The stated question — are round-lot orders retail flow profitable to trade against — bundles two claims: (1) round-lot size predicts retail origination, (2) trading against isolated retail flow earns money after costs. Most versions run these together, backtest an imbalance signal, and retrofit a retail story if it looks good — backwards, since round-lot imbalance can predict returns mechanically via order-flow imbalance with no retail content. This project tests claim (1) only, with a hard stop before any signal is built.

**H1:** round-lot size predicts retail origination with ≥2x lift over unconditional retail share, capturing ≥1/3 of retail volume, with above-chance signing accuracy. **H0 (my prior):** round lots are uninformative once venue is controlled for, because retail has moved to dollar-denominated/fractional orders (arriving as odd/mixed lots) while institutional VWAP/TWAP schedulers slice into 100-share children — making round lots closer to an institutional signature. If H0 holds, the deliverable is a well-evidenced negative result plus a map of better retail identifiers.

**Benchmarking (no ground truth exists; triangulate imperfect labels).** A — sub-penny price improvement on TRF prints (z = 100P − floor(100P); 0<z<0.4 retail sell, 0.6<z<1 retail buy): high precision, low recall, sign-error rates in the tens of percent, and broken by migration to midpoint pricing and the half-penny tick regime, so valid only pre-half-penny-compliance. B — exchange Retail Liquidity Program flags (NYSE, NYSE American, Arca, Cboe EDGX/BYX, Nasdaq, MEMX, IEX): near-1.0 precision by RMO certification, very low recall; must confirm which feeds carry the flag in historical (not just live) data. C — Rule 605 wholesaler reports (Citadel Securities, Virtu, G1X, Two Sigma, Jane Street, UBS), broken out by odd-lot/fractional/dollar buckets, paired with FINRA OTC transparency by MPID — cheap, spreadsheet-only, run first since it alone can kill the project. D (optional) — VandaTrack daily net retail buying as external confirmation.

**Data:** CRSP codes 10/11, NYSE/Nasdaq/NYSE American primary listing, $3–$600, ≥250k median daily volume (~2,000–2,500 names, size quintiles + $250+ bucket). 36 months ending before the half-penny compliance date. NYSE Daily TAQ trades + NBBO (nanosecond, full sale conditions), partitioned Parquet, DuckDB/Spark; exchange proprietary feeds for RLP flags; CRSP for returns. Compute round-lot status under both fixed-100 and the new tiered definition (100/40/10/1 shares by price tier). Sign lit trades via Lee-Ready, 1ms lag, checking robustness to zero-lag/tick test.

**Method:** partition by venue first (off-exchange TRF; lit w/ RLP; lit w/o RLP; off-exchange further split by NBBO position and sub-penny improvement) — never pool. Decompose round lots into exactly-100, multiples-of-100, and mixed lots. Five gate tests: G1 precision/lift (Rule 605 accounting + Hui-Walter latent-class estimate; kill if lift <2.0x or bootstrap lower bound <1.5x); G2 recall (kill <35%); G3 signing accuracy vs RLP-flagged known-side executions (kill <70%, hard stop <60%); G4 stock-day correlation vs Benchmark A (kill mean r<0.40) and vs D (kill <0.25); G5 panel regression of forward returns on Benchmark A imbalance + round-lot imbalance, double-clustered SEs (kill |t|<3). Plus two mechanism tests: price-elasticity of round-lot frequency (negative for RLP-flagged retail, flat for schedulers) and round-notional clustering ($100/$500/$1,000/$5,000) vs round-share clustering. Proceed to Phase 2 only if G1-G5 all pass in one partition. Phase 2 (conditional): build imbalance signal, test directional continuation (decile sorts, Fama-MacBeth) and liquidity-provision economics (spread decomposition); go/no-go at after-cost Sharpe ≥1.0, no negative year, net/gross >0.40.

**Pitfalls:** meme-stock window distorting the panel; stock splits; pre-2013 absence of odd lots from the tape; tiered round-lot and half-penny structural breaks; noisy-label understatement of agreement (motivating latent-class); multiple testing across partitions/benchmarks/horizons (pre-register thresholds, Benjamini-Hochberg); inconsistent fractional-share reporting across wholesalers; secular drift of "retail" toward systematic day-trading, eroding the premise even if identification succeeds.
